task.title: Multi-day live simulation audit: LLM appraisal fallback rates, output stability, and deterministic-path regression
task.objective: Write a test module that runs a multi-day simulation (3–5 days) with LLM appraisal active for T1/T2/T4, using mocked LLM responses to avoid real API calls, and asserts that fallback rates are within expected bounds, appraisal signals remain within valid ranges, deferred ticks always use the deterministic path, and the simulation completes without exceptions across all days.
task.exact_scope: One new test file at back/tests/test_p31_t6_multiday_audit.py. The test uses unittest.mock to patch appraisal_router.route so that: (a) some calls return a mocked successful LLM result (llm_used=True), (b) some calls return a mocked fallback result (llm_used=False), simulating realistic mixed behavior. The test drives simulate_day_bridged for 3–5 consecutive world days, collects AppraisalAuditLog entries from each day, and makes the assertions described in acceptance criteria. No modifications to engine files, router, or audit logger. No real LLM calls.
acceptance_criteria: A test asserts that simulate_day_bridged completes without raising an exception for each of at least 3 consecutive world days
A test asserts that across all days, the audit log contains entries only for tick types information_exposure, social_interaction, and relationship_shift (never T3/T5/T6/T7/T8 tick types)
A test asserts that the total count of audit log entries per day equals the number of active ticks attempted (T1 always present, T2 always present, T4 conditionally present based on world state)
A test asserts that LLM-path entries (llm_used=True) occur in at least one day's log when the mock is configured to return successful LLM output — confirming the LLM path is reachable
A test asserts that fallback entries (llm_used=False) occur when the mock is configured to simulate rejection — confirming fallback path is reachable
A test asserts that all AppraisalOutput values produced by LLM-path mock entries, when run through the settlement engine, produce numerically bounded state changes (no NaN, no out-of-range values)
A test asserts that the simulation result object returned from simulate_day_bridged each day exposes an audit_log attribute containing an AppraisalAuditLog instance
A test asserts that each AppraisalAuditEntry has a valid UTC ISO-8601 timestamp string in timestamp_iso

A test asserts that when 100% of route() calls fall back (mock always returns llm_used=False), the simulation still completes and produces valid final state — confirming graceful all-fallback operation
required_tests: Simulation completes without errors across 3 or more consecutive world days when LLM appraisal is mocked active
The audit log for each day records entries only for T1, T2, and T4 tick types — never for deferred ticks
At least one LLM-used entry appears when the mock is configured to succeed, confirming the LLM path executes
At least one fallback entry appears when the mock is configured to reject, confirming fallback path executes
Final agent state values after each day are numerically valid and within expected bounds after settlement
The simulation result exposes an audit_log containing an AppraisalAuditLog with correctly structured AppraisalAuditEntry records
Each audit entry carries a valid ISO-8601 UTC timestamp
When all route calls fall back (worst-case scenario), simulation completes and state remains coherent
non_goals: Making real LLM API calls or requiring an API key at test time
Testing the LLM prompt content or response quality
Activating T4 negative residual branches or modifying the T4 deterministic freeze
Modifying tick_bridge.py, appraisal_router.py, appraisal_audit_log.py, or any engine file
Producing a long-running integration harness — this is a standard pytest test file
constraints: No real LLM calls — all appraisal_router.route invocations must be patched with unittest.mock
AppraisalSignal v1 is frozen — tests must not modify or extend its field definitions
T4 deterministic path is frozen — tests must not attempt to activate T4 negative residual branches
Settlement is engine-authoritative — test assertions on numeric outcomes must not bypass settlement arithmetic
Deferred ticks T3/T5/T6/T7/T8 must never appear as LLM-used entries in the audit log
The test file must be independently runnable via: cd back && python -m pytest tests/test_p31_t6_multiday_audit.py -v
The test must not break any existing passing tests

execution_evidence.summary: Created back/tests/test_p31_t6_multiday_audit.py with 30 tests covering multi-day simulation audit: completion without errors, audit log tick type constraints, LLM/fallback path reachability, state bounds validation, audit_log attribute exposure, ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, and all-fallback scenario coherence.

## Round-0047 Summary — P31-T6

**Verdict: PASS**

### What was done
- **Designer** produced `task_contract.json` defining a multi-day simulation audit test using mocked LLM appraisal, with 9 concrete acceptance criteria covering tick type discipline, LLM/fallback path reachability, state bounds, timestamp validation, and all-fallback resilience.

- **Executor** created `back/tests/test_p31_t6_multiday_audit.py` — 30 tests across 8 test classes, all using `unittest.mock` to patch `appraisal_router.route` (no real LLM calls). Discovered and handled that `SimulationResult` uses `final_state`/`final_growth`/`final_relationships` field names.

- **Reviewer** confirmed all 9 acceptance criteria met, no forbidden files modified, and verified:
  - 30/30 new tests pass
  - 877/877 full suite passes (zero regressions)

### What was delivered
A comprehensive multi-day audit test that confirms the full P31 LLM appraisal integration is stable: the LLM path and fallback path are both reachable, deferred ticks never enter the LLM path, state remains bounded after settlement, and the simulation degrades gracefully under 100% fallback conditions.
